key_insight: The paper introduces ergoCub, a humanoid robot designed to optimize for both robot performance and human safety at the same time. By jointly tuning hardware and motion with human-aware metrics, it reduces spinal stress while improving walking robustness.
problem_solved: Traditional humanoid robots are often optimized mainly for locomotion performance, without adequately considering the physical burden or safety of nearby humans. This work addresses how to build and control humanoid robots that are more compatible with human bodies and safer in real-world environments.
method: Uses a shared embodied intelligence framework to co-optimize robot design and control.
Incorporates human-related metrics, such as back stress/spinal load, alongside locomotion objectives.
Tests the resulting ergoCub platform to evaluate safety-aware walking performance and robustness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how embodied intelligence can move beyond task success to include human-centered constraints. It highlights a practical path for building robots that are both effective and safer to deploy around people.

paper_title: Towards shared embodied intelligence in humanoid robots through optimization, development and testing of the human-aware ergoCub robot
paper_authors: Carlotta Sartore, Mohamed Elobaid, Lorenzo Rapetti, Giulio Romualdi, Stefano Dafarra
